newsitem.title: UK: BA denies plan to switch Heathrow routes.
newsitem.headline: BA denies plan to switch Heathrow routes.

text.p: British Airways Plc denied on Monday that it was planning to switch more British domestic routes from London Heathrow to London Gatwick in a move to garner more runway slots at Heathrow for its proposed transatlantic alliance with American Airlines.

Regional carrier Air Bristol said a decision by BA to move Plymouth and Newquay flights operated by its Brymon unit to Gatwick was likely to be followed by similar moves for flights to Belfast, Newcastle and Inverness as part of a grander plan to free up slots at Heathrow.

British Airways has been asked by British regulatory authorities to release 168 weekly, or 24 daily, takeoff and landing slots at Heathrow, the world's busiest international airport, to make room for more transatlantic competition as a condition for approving its deal with American.
"There is every indication that Belfast, Newcastle and Inverness could be next on BA's hit list," the Plymouth-based Air Bristol said in a statement.

BA denied this. "We have no plans to transfer these routes," said a spokesman. "Air Bristol seems to think this has got something to do with our proposed alliance with American. This is a completely separate issue," he said.
BA said the Brymon switch was an isolated decision designed to give Brymon room to expand London services.
Consequently Brymon is to increase frequencies from three to four a day from Newquay and four to five a day from Plymouth, with effect from March 30.

"It was Brymon's decision to move because they wanted to increase the number of services they offer from Plymouth and Newquay. They cannot do that at the times they want to at Heathrow but they can at Gatwick," the spokesman added.
